gen.title: Vacuum Free Fall and Galileo Observation

cards.stem: What does the page say about how a beach ball and an airliner fall in a vacuum?
cards.quote: In a vacuum, a beach ball falls with the same acceleration as an airliner.
cards.hint: Think about vacuum versus air conditions

cards.stem: Which sole external force acts on an object falling through a vacuum?
cards.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.
cards.hint: Recall what is absent in a vacuum

cards.stem: Which object properties are described as not affecting free fall description?
cards.quote: The weight, size, and shape of the object are not a factor in describing a free fall.
cards.hint: Focus on properties said to be irrelevant

cards.stem: Who was first credited with the observation that free falling objects fall at equal rate?
cards.quote: The remarkable observation that all free falling objects fall at the same rate was first proposed by Galileo, nearly 400 years ago.
cards.hint: Recall the early investigator of inclined planes
